route_title: Check and test your change where you live
can_skip: Exploring a change where you live? This path replaces Parts 3, 4 and 5.
intro_title: Exploring a change where you live? This path replaces Parts 3, 4 and 5.
intro: Many changes happen where you already are: fewer working days, another job, your own business, more space, another home in the same area, more time outside. They change your money, your week and the people around you, just like a move does. This path checks that kind of change with the same care a mover gives a new country.
Start with the change you chose in Step 1: your staying option from Part 4, or the direction in your Working Direction. Use Parts 1 and 2 only if the place might change too. Then come back here.

exercises.title: The money check at the changed income
intro: Redo your First Money Picture from Step 1 for the change. Use the income you would have after it: four days instead of five, a new salary, or the first year of your own business. As in Step 1, count confirmed and agreed income. Hoped income stays out.

row_labels: Left over or short each month
One-time costs of the change: a course, equipment, a gap in income
Savings I keep as a reserve

tips: Short each month after the change? That is not the end of the idea. It shows what to work on: lower costs, more certain income, or a later start. Step 3 checks the money again with your runway.

exercises.title: The rules at work or at home
intro: A change where you live has rules too. They come from your contract, your employer, your landlord or your municipality. Write down what applies to your change, where you found it, and when.

row_labels: What does my contract or employer allow: fewer hours, remote work, unpaid leave?
Notice periods or deadlines I must respect
Do I need to register a business, or tell the tax office?
Do I need permission for a change at home: renting out, building, a business from home?
What does it mean for my pension, insurance or benefits?
Who can I ask: HR, an accountant, the council?

watch_out: This is expert work. Working fewer hours or starting a business can change your tax, your pension and your social security. Ask your employer, your pension fund or an adviser before you sign anything.

exercises.title: Time: who decides your week after the change?
intro: In Step 1 you sorted your week into time fixed by others, must do's and your own choice. Do it again for the week after the change. A change can free time, but it can also bring new must do's: a business to run, a course, more admin.

row_labels: New must do's this change brings

exercises.title: The people involved
intro: Talk to the people this change touches: your partner, your children, a manager, colleagues, clients or friends. Ask what it means for them and what they would need. Then find one person who already made a change like yours, and ask: what did you underestimate?

columns.label: What this change means for them

exercises.title: Test your change in real life
intro: A visit tests a place. For a change where you live, you test the change itself: small, for a limited time, and before you commit. A good test is cheap and quick, and it can prove you wrong.
bullets: Work four days for a month, using a holiday day each week.
Take one afternoon a week outside for six weeks.
Sell at a local market on three Saturdays before you start a business.
Live on your future income for two months, and save the difference.

example.text: For six weeks, I took Friday afternoon off as unpaid leave and spent it outside. Our budget held. By week three, the errands had moved into Friday, so the time was only half mine. Next test: Friday stays outside, and the errands move to Thursday evening.

result_guide.intro: All four answers are good ones:
rows: Step 3 checks it with the five green lights and ends with your Change Plan.
One more test is cheaper than a decision you have to undo. Set the end date now.
Look at a move after all
If the test showed that your change needs another place, go back to Part 1 or 2 with what you learned.
